text:
mike: Hey team, customer acct 9142 hitting intermittent parse failures in JSON mode. They send the same prompt and see valid JSON ~60% of the time, other times model returns a prose sentence or trailing comma -> JSON.parse errors. Repro steps attached below.

tara: thanks, mike. can you paste the exact request/response example? also send request_id from the failed call if you have it.

mike: request_id=f7a9c2b3. curl we used: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-infer-prod-1","mode":"json","prompt":"Generate JSON list of products...","max_tokens":350}'
```

mike: sample bad response (got returned in response.body):
```
Sorry, I can't do that right now.\n{"products": [ {"id": "p1","name": "Widget"}, ]}
```

lev: aha — looks like wrapper text + trailing comma. two issues: extra prose before JSON and a trailing comma inside array. both break strict parsers.

tara: do we have a recommended repair flow for this customer? they run strict schema validation downstream.

lev: suggest multilayer approach: 1) re-ask (short constraint prompt) 2) self-heal regex extraction 3) fallback parse-with-lenient-json then strict validation + report. Add exponential backoff for retries if it's rate/latency related.

sophia: concrete re-ask example i used before: 
```
Please respond ONLY with a single valid JSON object. Do NOT include any extraneous text. If you cannot produce valid JSON, return {"error":"unavailable"}.
```

lev: for regex cleanup we typically try: extract first brace block with balanced braces then run a tidy step: remove trailing commas with `re.sub(r",\s*([}\]])","\1", text)` then attempt json.loads. If that still fails, escalate.

mike: customer reports this started after they enabled streaming + low max_tokens (200). Could streaming truncation be causing protruding text?

ops: streaming can lead to partial responses if connection interrupted. check logs for http_status for request_id f7a9c2b3 and client disconnects. i'll pull perf logs.

support-bot: log entry for f7a9c2b3: status=200 generated, connection_closed_by_client=true, latency_ms=4200.

tara: that matches truncated stream theory. best immediate step: implement "finalize" re-ask with the model (idempotent) — send original prompt + last partial output + instruction: "Complete the partial JSON and output only valid JSON object." Use 1 retry then regex cleanup then mark as repaired.

lev: retry policy idea: attempt immediate re-ask (no wait) up to 2 times, then exponential backoff 1s, 2s, 4s with jitter for subsequent retries. add circuit-breaker if >5 failures in 60s for this customer to avoid extra cost.

mike: will propose to customer: implement client-side lenient extractor that first attempts to find balanced {} or [] blocks, apply trailing-comma strip, then if still invalid, call backend repair endpoint (we can provide a small prompt template).

tara: please include the repair prompt template in the ticket. mike, can you paste it here and I'll attach to the Zendesk ticket?

mike: repair prompt we recommend: 
```
You are a JSON fixer. Input may contain extra text or be truncated. Extract the first valid JSON structure from the input, fix common problems (remove trailing commas, close unbalanced brackets/braces), and output ONLY the corrected JSON. If you cannot safely fix it, output {"error":"cannot_fix"}.
```

lev: also include a note: if truncation is frequent, suggest customer increase max_tokens or disable streaming for critical parsing flows, or add client-side buffering to ensure complete transmission.

tara: escalation action items: mike -> add repair prompt/template to ticket; ops -> verify connection_closed_by_client pattern for 9142 last 48h; support -> send code snippets for regex cleanup + backoff pseudocode. I'll follow up with the customer. :thumbsup:

mike: added template to ticket and pasted regex snippet. tagging ops for logs: @ops

ops: got it, I'm pulling full trace and will DM with correlation id.

sophia: small note on safety — repair prompts must avoid hallucinating missing required fields. instruct repair to NOT invent new items; just fix syntax. include that in template.

mike: good call. updated template in ticket. thanks all.
